In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data structures we have presented are able to maintain the separator of threshold graphs and of difference graphs under edge insertions and deletions in amortized constant time.
, for both threshold and difference graphs we can efficiently maintain the value of the minimum separator.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show how to maintain a separator for a dynamic graph in time proportional to the number of changes in the graph, and how to use the data structure to perform the operations on the graph in linear time.
we provide a data structure that maintains the minimality of a separator of a threshold graph, and can answer queries about the graph in constant time, in the fully dynamic case.
we provide a data structure for maintaining the minimum value of the separator for threshold graphs, which is able to support all the operations in O(1) amortized time, with O(n) space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the separator is not just an interesting theoretical object, but can be used to maintain the minimality of a threshold or difference graph in a dynamic setting.
